novelty_flags.label: All statement consumer fields
novelty_flags.one_line: Consumers remain generic—for example, thm:rank-zero-local-experiment says “Researchers deciding whether…,” thm:uniform-rank-adaptive-inference says “An applied causal study,” and oeq:gaussian-optimal-calibration says “causal efficiency diagnostics”—rather than naming a DiD/DDD application domain, published workflow, or open problem.

soundness_flags.label: thm:rank-zero-local-experiment
soundness_flags.one_line: IID sampling, asymptotic linearity, covariance convergence, and experiment-level LAN do not by themselves yield the displayed Gaussian limit for this particular estimator; add a uniform Lindeberg/joint estimator-limit condition or state that convergence directly.

soundness_flags.label: thm:uniform-rank-adaptive-inference
soundness_flags.one_line: The supremum and infimum range over unspecified P_n even though assumptions are only “over the stated local paths,” and “local null geometry is consistently selected” has no defined selection event or regime.

soundness_flags.label: Core target fields
soundness_flags.one_line: target_estimand is τ(P_n), while every inferential headline targets Δ(θ_n); identify Δ as the statistical target and τ as the underlying causal contrast, or add a theorem linking the reported procedure to inference on τ.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:rank-zero-local-experiment and thm:uniform-rank-adaptive-inference / technical_internal_limitation
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Applications must supply a regular asymptotically linear reduced-form estimator for (K,a), covariance consistency, and a valid multiplier approximation; these results do not derive them from an estimated singular covariance square root.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The accepted claim is conditional rank-adaptive inference for applications with the stated regular reduced form, not an automatic theorem for every estimated Ω.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: honest_scope / all gain statements
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The optimization is restricted to a declared finite retained-score affine span and does not characterize the full observed-data canonical gradient or semiparametric efficiency bound.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The field-tier claim concerns a finite-span causal-score variance gain only.

source_verification_receipts.version: Review of Economic Studies 86(1), 2019, version of record
source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and Introduction, pp. 377–380; especially equations (1)–(3) and Section 3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies inference for a known directionally differentiable map φ of an estimable parameter, proves standard-bootstrap failure absent full differentiability under Gaussian limits, and proposes derivative-aware resampling with local size analysis.

source_verification_receipts.version: Journal of Econometrics 210(2), 2019, version of record
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper develops a unified inference framework for a fixed known functional with null first derivative, including second-order bootstrap procedures and standard-bootstrap failure under first-order degeneracy.
The paper tests H0: rank(Π0)≤r, accommodates true rank below the boundary rank, and constructs nonstandard bootstrap critical values with two-step tuning for size control and power improvement.

The paper establishes behavior of estimators, tests, and confidence sets over weak, semi-strong, and strong identification sequences for criterion-based models, including uniform asymptotic size results.

The paper defines weakly regular semiparametric parameters, establishes impossibility of consistent or equivariant estimation in that setting, and characterizes them through underlying regular parameters.

source_verification_receipts.version: Asymptotic Statistics, Chapter 7, Cambridge University Press, 1998
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The cited chapters define LAN, show convergence to Gaussian experiments after local rescaling, and explain limit-experiment implications for testing and estimation.
